verses.latin: In principio creavit Deus cælum et terram.

english.text: In the beginning God created heaven, and earth.

verses.latin: Terra autem erat inanis et vacua, et tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi : et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.

english.text: And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of God moved over the waters.

verses.latin: Dixitque Deus : Fiat lux. Et facta est lux.

english.text: And God said: Be light made. And light was made.

verses.latin: Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona : et divisit lucem a tenebris.

english.text: And God saw the light that it was good; and he divided the light from the darkness.

verses.latin: Appellavitque lucem Diem, et tenebras Noctem : factumque est vespere et mane, dies unus.

english.text: And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night; and there was evening and morning one day.

verses.latin: Dixit quoque Deus : Fiat firmamentum in medio aquarum : et dividat aquas ab aquis.

english.text: And God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.

verses.latin: Et fecit Deus firmamentum, divisitque aquas, quæ erant sub firmamento, ab his, quæ erant super firmamentum. Et factum est ita.

english.text: And God made a firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those that were above the firmament, and it was so.

verses.latin: Vocavitque Deus firmamentum, Cælum : et factum est vespere et mane, dies secundus.

english.text: And God called the firmament, Heaven; and the evening and morning were the second day.

verses.latin: Dixit vero Deus : Congregentur aquæ, quæ sub cælo sunt, in locum unum : et appareat arida. Et factum est ita.

english.text: God also said: Let the waters that are under the heaven, be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done.

verses.latin: Et vocavit Deus aridam Terram, congregationesque aquarum appellavit Maria. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

english.text: And God called the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.

verses.latin: Et ait : Germinet terra herbam virentem, et facientem semen, et lignum pomiferum faciens fructum juxta genus suum, cujus semen in semetipso sit super terram. Et factum est ita.

english.text: And he said: Let the earth bring forth the green herb, and such as may seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, which may have seed in itself upon the earth. And it was so done.

verses.latin: Et protulit terra herbam virentem, et facientem semen juxta genus suum, lignumque faciens fructum, et habens unumquodque sementem secundum speciem suam. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

english.text: And the earth brought forth the green herb, and such as yieldeth seed according to its kind, and the tree that beareth fruit having seed each one according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.latin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies tertius.

english.text: And the evening and the morning were the third day.

verses.latin: Dixit autem Deus : Fiant luminaria in firmamento cæli, et dividant diem ac noctem, et sint in signa et tempora, et dies et annos :

english.text: And God said: Let there be lights made in the firmament of heaven, to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:

verses.latin: ut luceant in firmamento cæli, et illuminent terram. Et factum est ita.

english.text: To shine in the firmament of heaven, and to give light upon the earth. And it was so done.

verses.latin: Fecitque Deus duo luminaria magna : luminare majus, ut præesset diei : et luminare minus, ut præesset nocti : et stellas.

english.text: And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day; and a lesser light to rule the night: and the stars.

verses.latin: Et posuit eas in firmamento cæli, ut lucerent super terram,

english.text: And he set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth.

verses.latin: et præessent diei ac nocti, et dividerent lucem ac tenebras. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

english.text: And to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

verses.latin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies quartus.

english.text: And the evening and morning were the fourth day.

verses.latin: Dixit etiam Deus : Producant aquæ reptile animæ viventis, et volatile super terram sub firmamento cæli.

english.text: God also said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping creature having life, and the fowl that may fly over the earth under the firmament of heaven.

verses.latin: Creavitque Deus cete grandia, et omnem animam viventem atque motabilem, quam produxerant aquæ in species suas, et omne volatile secundum genus suum. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

english.text: And God created the great whales, and every living and moving creature, which the waters brought forth, according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.latin: Benedixitque eis, dicens : Crescite, et multiplicamini, et replete aquas maris : avesque multiplicentur super terram.

english.text: And he blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters of the sea: and let the birds be multiplied upon the earth.

verses.latin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies quintus.

english.text: And the evening and morning were the fifth day.

verses.latin: Dixit quoque Deus : Producat terra animam viventem in genere suo, jumenta, et reptilia, et bestias terræ secundum species suas. Factumque est ita.

english.text: And God said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, according to their kinds. And it was so done.

verses.latin: Et fecit Deus bestias terræ juxta species suas, et jumenta, et omne reptile terræ in genere suo. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum,

english.text: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and cattle, and every thing that creepeth on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.latin: et ait : Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram : et præsit piscibus maris, et volatilibus cæli, et bestiis, universæque terræ, omnique reptili, quod movetur in terra.

english.text: And he said: Let us make man to our image and likeness: and let him have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and the beasts, and the whole earth, and every creeping creature that moveth upon the earth.

verses.latin: Et creavit Deus hominem ad imaginem suam : ad imaginem Dei creavit illum, masculum et feminam creavit eos.

english.text: And God created man to his own image: to the image of God he created him: male and female he created them.

verses.latin: Benedixitque illis Deus, et ait : Crescite et multiplicamini, et replete terram, et subjicite eam, et dominamini piscibus maris, et volatilibus cæli, et universis animantibus, quæ moventur super terram.

english.text: And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and all living creatures that move upon the earth.

verses.latin: Dixitque Deus : Ecce dedi vobis omnem herbam afferentem semen super terram, et universa ligna quæ habent in semetipsis sementem generis sui, ut sint vobis in escam :

english.text: And God said: Behold I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the earth, and all trees that have in themselves seed of their own kind, to be your meat:

verses.latin: et cunctis animantibus terræ, omnique volucri cæli, et universis quæ moventur in terra, et in quibus est anima vivens, ut habeant ad vescendum. Et factum est ita.

english.text: And to all the beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so done.

verses.latin: Viditque Deus cuncta quæ fecerat, et erant valde bona. Et factum est vespere et mane, dies sextus.

english.text: And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good. And the evening and morning were the sixth day.

verses.latin: Igitur perfecti sunt cæli et terra, et omnis ornatus eorum.

english.text: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them.

verses.latin: Complevitque Deus die septimo opus suum quod fecerat : et requievit die septimo ab universo opere quod patrarat.

english.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.

verses.latin: Et benedixit diei septimo, et sanctificavit illum, quia in ipso cessaverat ab omni opere suo quod creavit Deus ut faceret.

english.text: And he blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

verses.latin: Istæ sunt generationes cæli et terræ, quando creata sunt, in die quo fecit Dominus Deus cælum et terram,

english.text: These are the generations of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth:

verses.latin: et omne virgultum agri antequam oriretur in terra, omnemque herbam regionis priusquam germinaret : non enim pluerat Dominus Deus super terram, et homo non erat qui operaretur terram :

english.text: And every plant of the field before it spring up in the earth, and every herb of the ground before it grew: for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth; and there was not a man to till the earth.

verses.latin: sed fons ascendebat e terra, irrigans universam superficiem terræ.

english.text: But a spring rose out the earth, watering all the surface of the earth.

verses.latin: Formavit igitur Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ, et inspiravit in faciem ejus spiraculum vitæ, et factus est homo in animam viventem.

english.text: And the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul.

verses.latin: Plantaverat autem Dominus Deus paradisum voluptatis a principio, in quo posuit hominem quem formaverat.

english.text: And the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure from the beginning: wherein he placed man whom he had formed.

verses.latin: Produxitque Dominus Deus de humo omne lignum pulchrum visu, et ad vescendum suave lignum etiam vitæ in medio paradisi, lignumque scientiæ boni et mali.

english.text: And the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold, and pleasant to eat of: the tree of life also in the midst of paradise: and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

verses.latin: Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis ad irrigandum paradisum, qui inde dividitur in quatuor capita.

english.text: And a river went out the place of pleasure to water paradise, which from thence is divided into four heads.

verses.latin: Nomen uni Phison : ipse est qui circuit omnem terram Hevilath, ubi nascitur aurum :

english.text: The name of the one is Phison: that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath, where gold groweth.

verses.latin: et aurum terræ illius optimum est ; ibi invenitur bdellium, et lapis onychinus.

english.text: And the gold of that land is very good: there is found bdellium, and the onyx stone.

verses.latin: Et nomen fluvii secundi Gehon ; ipse est qui circumit omnem terram Æthiopiæ.

english.text: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia

verses.latin: Nomen vero fluminis tertii, Tigris : ipse vadit contra Assyrios. Fluvius autem quartus, ipse est Euphrates.

english.text: And the name of the third river is Tigris: the same passeth along by the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates.

verses.latin: Tulit ergo Dominus Deus hominem, et posuit eum in paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur, et custodiret illum :

english.text: And the Lord God took man, and put him into the paradise for pleasure, to dress it, and keep it.

verses.latin: præcepitque ei, dicens : Ex omni ligno paradisi comede ;

english.text: And he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat:

verses.latin: de ligno autem scientiæ boni et mali ne comedas : in quocumque enim die comederis ex eo, morte morieris.

english.text: But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat. for in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death.

verses.latin: Dixit quoque Dominus Deus : Non est bonum esse hominem solum : faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi.

english.text: And the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself.

verses.latin: Formatis igitur Dominus Deus de humo cunctis animantibus terræ, et universis volatilibus cæli, adduxit ea ad Adam, ut videret quid vocaret ea : omne enim quod vocavit Adam animæ viventis, ipsum est nomen ejus.

english.text: And the Lord God having formed out of the ground all the beasts of the earth, and all the fowls of the air, brought them to Adam to see what he would call them: for whatsoever Adam called any living creature the same is its name.

verses.latin: Appellavitque Adam nominibus suis cuncta animantia, et universa volatilia cæli, et omnes bestias terræ : Adæ vero non inveniebatur adjutor similis ejus.

english.text: And Adam called all the beasts by their names, and all the fowls of the air, and all the cattle of the field: but for Adam there was not found a helper like himself.

verses.latin: Immisit ergo Dominus Deus soporem in Adam : cumque obdormisset, tulit unam de costis ejus, et replevit carnem pro ea.

english.text: Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam: and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh for it.

verses.latin: Et ædificavit Dominus Deus costam, quam tulerat de Adam, in mulierem : et adduxit eam ad Adam.

english.text: And the Lord God built the rib which he took from Adam into a woman: and brought her to Adam.

verses.latin: Dixitque Adam : Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea : hæc vocabitur Virago, quoniam de viro sumpta est.

english.text: And Adam said: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man.

verses.latin: Quam ob rem relinquet homo patrem suum, et matrem, et adhærebit uxori suæ : et erunt duo in carne una.

english.text: Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh.

verses.latin: Erat autem uterque nudus, Adam scilicet et uxor ejus : et non erubescebant.

english.text: And they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed.

verses.latin: Sed et serpens erat callidior cunctis animantibus terræ quæ fecerat Dominus Deus. Qui dixit ad mulierem : Cur præcepit vobis Deus ut non comederetis de omni ligno paradisi ?

english.text: Now the serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth which the Lord God made. And he said to the woman: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?

verses.latin: Cui respondit mulier : De fructu lignorum, quæ sunt in paradiso, vescimur :

english.text: And the woman answered him, saying: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:

verses.latin: de fructu vero ligni quod est in medio paradisi, præcepit nobis Deus ne comederemus, et ne tangeremus illud, ne forte moriamur.

english.text: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath commanded us that we should not eat; and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.

verses.latin: Dixit autem serpens ad mulierem : Nequaquam morte moriemini.

english.text: And the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death.

verses.latin: Scit enim Deus quod in quocumque die comederitis ex eo, aperientur oculi vestri, et eritis sicut dii, scientes bonum et malum.

english.text: For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.

verses.latin: Vidit igitur mulier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescendum, et pulchrum oculis, aspectuque delectabile : et tulit de fructu illius, et comedit : deditque viro suo, qui comedit.

english.text: And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave to her husband who did eat.

verses.latin: Et aperti sunt oculi amborum ; cumque cognovissent se esse nudos, consuerunt folia ficus, et fecerunt sibi perizomata.

english.text: And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons.

verses.latin: Et cum audissent vocem Domini Dei deambulantis in paradiso ad auram post meridiem, abscondit se Adam et uxor ejus a facie Domini Dei in medio ligni paradisi.

english.text: And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God, amidst the trees of paradise.

verses.latin: Vocavitque Dominus Deus Adam, et dixit ei : Ubi es ?

english.text: And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?

verses.latin: Qui ait : Vocem tuam audivi in paradiso, et timui, eo quod nudus essem, et abscondi me.

english.text: And he said: I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.

verses.latin: Cui dixit : Quis enim indicavit tibi quod nudus esses, nisi quod ex ligno de quo præceperam tibi ne comederes, comedisti ?

english.text: And he said to him: And who hath told thee that thou wast naked, but that thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?

verses.latin: Dixitque Adam : Mulier, quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi.

english.text: And Adam said: The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

verses.latin: Et dixit Dominus Deus ad mulierem : Quare hoc fecisti ? Quæ respondit : Serpens decepit me, et comedi.

english.text: And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.

verses.latin: Et ait Dominus Deus ad serpentem : Quia fecisti hoc, maledictus es inter omnia animantia, et bestias terræ : super pectus tuum gradieris, et terram comedes cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.

english.text: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because thou hast done this thing, thou art cursed among all cattle, and the beasts of the earth: upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.

verses.latin: Inimicitias ponam inter te et mulierem, et semen tuum et semen illius : ipsa conteret caput tuum, et tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus.

english.text: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.

verses.latin: Mulieri quoque dixit : Multiplicabo ærumnas tuas, et conceptus tuos : in dolore paries filios, et sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui.

english.text: To the woman also he said: I will multiply thy sorrows, and thy conceptions: in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children, and thou shalt be under thy husband's power, and he shall have dominion over thee.

verses.latin: Adæ vero dixit : Quia audisti vocem uxoris tuæ, et comedisti de ligno, ex quo præceperam tibi ne comederes, maledicta terra in opere tuo : in laboribus comedes ex ea cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.

english.text: And to Adam he said: Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat, cursed is the earth in thy work; with labour and toil shalt thou eat thereof all the days of thy life.

verses.latin: Spinas et tribulos germinabit tibi, et comedes herbam terræ.

english.text: Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou eat the herbs of the earth.

verses.latin: In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane, donec revertaris in terram de qua sumptus es : quia pulvis es et in pulverem reverteris.

english.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth, out of which thou wast taken: for dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

verses.latin: Et vocavit Adam nomen uxoris suæ, Heva : eo quod mater esset cunctorum viventium.

english.text: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve: because she was the mother of all the living.

verses.latin: Fecit quoque Dominus Deus Adæ et uxori ejus tunicas pelliceas, et induit eos :

english.text: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife, garments of skins, and clothed them.

verses.latin: et ait : Ecce Adam quasi unus ex nobis factus est, sciens bonum et malum : nunc ergo ne forte mittat manum suam, et sumat etiam de ligno vitæ, et comedat, et vivat in æternum.

english.text: And he said: Behold Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever.

verses.latin: Et emisit eum Dominus Deus de paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur terram de qua sumptus est.

english.text: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.

verses.latin: Ejecitque Adam : et collocavit ante paradisum voluptatis cherubim, et flammeum gladium, atque versatilem, ad custodiendam viam ligni vitæ.

english.text: And he cast out Adam; and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

verses.latin: Et ait Dominus ad Cain : Ubi est Abel frater tuus ? Qui respondit : Nescio : num custos fratris mei sum ego ?

english.text: And the Lord said to Cain: Where is thy brother Abel? And he answered, I know not: am I my brother's keeper?

verses.latin: Dixitque Lot ad eos : Quæso, domine mi,

english.text: And Lot said to them: I beseech thee my Lord,

verses.latin: Hi sunt filii Cham in cognationibus, et linguis, et generationibus, terrisque et gentibus suis.

english.text: These are the children of Cham in their kindreds, and tongues, and generations, and lands, and nations.

verses.latin: terramque quam dedi Abraham et Isaac, dabo tibi et semini tuo post te.

english.text: And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to thee, and to thy seed after thee.
